# 0073: A tool call is timed, and costed both as issued and as carried in context, and so is the skill under test

Status: accepted, 2026-10-18.
Extends [0022](0022-record-kind-catalogue-and-skill-coverage.md) (skill coverage), whose file accesses each skill event names.
Extends [0065](0065-a-subagent-is-priced-at-its-own-models-rates.md) (each thread at its own model's rates) and [0072](0072-every-subagent-is-linked-to-its-spawn-or-the-fold-stops.md) (every thread is linked).
So a subagent's tool calls are priced and placed like the primary's.

## Context

A run recorded which tools each turn issued, but not when each ran, how long it took or what it cost.
Skill coverage recorded which turns touched each skill file, but not when the skill came into use, for how long, or at what cost.
Neither provider bills a tool call, so no log reports one's cost.
A tool's result is billed again on every later call that carries it, and from the prompt cache that charge is small but repeated.

## Decision

**A tool call is timed from its log.** `ToolCall.started_at` is the record that issued it and `ended_at` the record of its result, matched by tool-use id.
`duration_ms` is the gap between them.
A tool whose result was never logged has no end, never a guessed one.

**A tool call is costed two ways, side by side.** `issuing_cost_usd` is the billed cost of the model call that asked for it, split evenly across the tools that call issued.
`context_cost_usd` is what carrying its result cost.
The result's tokens are estimated from its characters, four to a token.
That estimate is bounded by the prompt growth measured at the call that first read it.
At each call from then on, the result is charged its share of that call's prompt cost.
The charges stop at the first call whose prompt is smaller than where the result entered, which is a compaction.
Each charge is kept as a per-turn `trace`, so its downstream impact can be followed turn by turn.
`cache_rereads` counts the later calls that re-read it from the prompt cache.

**Every thread's tool calls are costed at that thread's model's rates.** `derive/toolcost.py` writes `RunResult.tool_costs`, one `ToolCost` per tool call of the primary and of every subagent, after pricing.

**The skill under test has a span and a cost.** `RunResult.skill_use` starts at its first trigger.
That is the run's first turn when the run's own invocation named the skill, else the first tool call that touched one of its files.
The span ends at the last such touch.
Its totals sum each tool call that touched a skill file once.
Its `events` list every access, with the figures of the tool call that made it.
A command Codex's shell reports running is credited to its turn's shell tool when that turn issued exactly one, and carries no figures otherwise.

## Consequences

A session shows when every tool ran, how long it took, what it cost to ask for and what its output cost to keep.
A small result read early can be seen costing more than a large one read late.

Both costs are attributions, not bills, and they overlap: an issuing call's prompt already carries earlier results.
Neither is summed into the run's estimate, which stays the billed total.
The token estimate is bounded by what was measured but is still an estimate, and the page says so.

## Lens

Providers bill tokens, never tools, so a tool's cost is an attribution.
Make it two ways and name both: what it cost to ask for, and what its output cost to keep.
